transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in to see me?

Ever since that robbery, I keep organizing my whole life around avoiding anything that reminds me of it—certain neighborhoods, late meetings, even some community events. It’s gotten to the point where I realize I'm arranging my entire schedule just to feel safe, and a close friend suggested I finally come speak to someone.

Since the robbery, do you also have nightmares, flashbacks, or sudden intense distress when something reminds you of it? Or is the main problem fear of going out or being in places where escape might be hard?

It’s actually both. I have intense flashbacks where I suddenly feel like I'm back on the floor with a gun to my head and my chest gets incredibly tight, especially when I'm locking up or hear a loud male voice. To cope, I actively avoid certain areas, late meetings, and parking garages, and I find myself constantly scanning for exits and watching who is around me.
Do you also have persistent nightmares, intrusive memories, or feel emotionally numb or on edge since the robbery, even when you are not in places you fear?

Yes, I feel constantly on edge—I'm always scanning exits, jumping at sudden noises, and waking up in the middle of the night with my heart racing. I also feel this deep emotional numbness, like I'm watching my loved ones from behind glass, and the things that used to bring me joy now just feel completely flat.

When you avoid places like parking garages or late meetings, is it mainly because you fear having another panic-like episode or being unable to escape or get help, rather than because they remind you of the robbery itself?

No, it is definitely because those situations remind me of the robbery itself. Being in a parking garage or out late at night brings back that overwhelming feeling of vulnerability and danger, making my skin crawl because it feels like I'm putting myself right back in harm's way. It isn't about fearing a panic attack; it's about feeling completely unsafe.
How long have these symptoms been going on since the robbery—has it been more than one month?

Yes, it has been much longer than a month. These feelings started a few months after the robbery and have been going on steadily for well over a year now. It has been hanging over my life for a very long time.
Have these symptoms been present for more than one month, and did they start after the robbery?
Yes, they definitely started after the robbery, beginning about a few months after it happened. They have been with me steadily ever since, which is well over a year now.
Since the robbery, do you ever have moments where you feel detached from yourself or like the world around you is unreal, as if you are watching everything happen from outside your body?

No, I don't feel like I'm outside of my own body or that the physical world itself isn't real. While I do feel socially disconnected from other people—like I'm watching them from behind glass—I still feel physically present in myself.
Do you ever have episodes where you lose time, feel like you are outside your body, or feel as if the world around you is unreal?

I don't lose time in my day-to-day life, though I do have blank spots in my memory about the night of the robbery itself, and I don't feel literally outside my body. However, the world can feel a bit unreal because I often feel so detached from other people. It’s like I'm watching everyone from behind glass rather than actually participating in the moment.
Do you still have unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks of the robbery that come back even when you try not to think about it?

Yes, I do. Out of nowhere, like when I'm locking up or hear a loud male voice, I'll suddenly see myself back on that floor with the gun at my head, and my chest tightens so much I can't breathe. Even at night, my mind constantly replays that night, keeping me awake for hours with my heart racing.
